channel.title: The New Yorker — Reporting
channel.description: Latest reporting from The New Yorker

item.title: The Fallout of a Charlie Kirk Campus Scandal
item.description: Students and faculty across the country were punished for their reactions to the conservative activist’s murder. A recent graduate of Texas Tech’s law school is still trying to clear her name.

item.title: Is A.I. Above the Law?
item.description: Our legal system isn’t ready for machines that act on their own.

item.title: Hockey Dads and Hockey Sons
item.description: Parenting is a practice. You learn from your mistakes and then repeat them anyway.

item.title: Should I Stay or Should I Go?
item.description: The quandary faced by government lawyers who think that the Trump Administration is subverting justice.

item.title: How Paweł Pawlikowski Learned to Film Europe’s Fractures
item.description: The Polish director has made a career out of examining the mysteries of borders, both spiritual and political.

item.title: Why Doesn’t Anyone Want to Fix One of America’s Scariest Roads?
item.description: The Million Dollar Highway, prone to rockfall and avalanches, is the site of horrific crashes and courageous rescues.

item.title: The Battle to Pass a Billionaire Tax
item.description: Most Democratic voters say that they favor a wealth tax, but a California ballot initiative has plenty of liberal opponents.

item.title: The Battle for the Post-Trump Right
item.description: For decades, the Heritage Foundation was a conservative powerhouse. Can it stay relevant in the influencer age?

item.title: Year of the Horse
item.description: After a young tourist was killed in a Central Park carriage accident this summer, the City Council is considering whether to ban horse-drawn carriages forever.

item.title: A Self-Made Woman
item.description: My cousin Laura had a diva’s charisma and a siren’s voice. She also had a mysterious past. When she died, she left me to tell the story of her defiant reinvention.
